timeline.public-api.surface.rationale: Timeline public exports remain consumable by the route surface.

timeline.strip.math.rationale: Range URL transitions preserve server-owned millisecond bounds.

timeline.shared.presentation.rationale: Shared event markers retain their semantic presentation.

timeline.filters.url.rationale: Toolbar filters serialize canonically and restore with browser history.

timeline.lanes.presentation.rationale: Lane grouping and order are rendered from the authorized projection.

timeline.live.stream.rationale: Live frame merging preserves bounded snapshot identity and ordering.

timeline.list.detail.rationale: List events open the detail sheet without losing selected-event URL state.

timeline.strip.controls.rationale: Range picker, lens controls, keyboard navigation, and reduced motion are exercised at the route surface.

timeline.swimlanes.grouping.rationale: Swimlane grouping, sorting, and pin affordances remain capability-gated.

timeline.toolbar.controls.rationale: Toolbar controls expose only server-described choices and preserve focus behavior.

timeline.toolbar.state.rationale: Activity and problem projections map to stable URL filter state.

timeline.adapter.source.rationale: The adapter maps authenticated snapshot, overview, and stream contracts without source-runtime imports.

timeline.local-scrubber.rationale: Local source selection remains route-capability gated.

timeline.retained-overview.rationale: Retained overview buckets and coverage are created from an authorized server aggregation.

timeline.view.integration.rationale: Timeline view controls compose through the product surface rather than the upstream runtime.

timeline.url.history.rationale: Back, forward, replace-history, and deep-link state use one URL state model.

timeline.source-context.rationale: Source selection and transport composition remain isolated in the product adapter.

timeline.source-contract.rationale: HTTP capability, snapshot, overview, and stream request shapes are validated at the product boundary.

applications.catalog.batch-runtime.rationale: Catalog cards and table rows must render batch runtime, retained run outcome, and deterministic attention ordering from a typed product projection.

applications.catalog.delivery-status.rationale: The adapter must keep runtime readiness and deployment-source delivery state distinct instead of deriving either in the browser.

applications.detail.scope-tabs.rationale: Application, workload, and detail-tab URL state must round-trip through one route controller without mounting the wrong scope.

applications.detail.overview-projection.rationale: The Python response schema must make source, workload, batch, relationship, and completeness evidence explicit before the overview can render it.

applications.detail.topology.rationale: Authorized application topology, workload focus, resource navigation, and source-inventory differences require route-level interaction coverage.

applications.detail.history.rationale: Authorized application history must preserve partial-source evidence, deployment anchors, incidents, and source links without exposing provider payloads.

applications.detail.identity-switcher.rationale: Environment-instance switching, popover dismissal, focus, and reduced-motion behavior must be exercised in the product route.

applications.detail.parity.rationale: The existing generic five-tab detail test is expanded into application-detail parity coverage only after its typed projection exists.

applications.public-api.rationale: The route-level application tab and workload-scope contract remains consumable without importing the isolated upstream component barrel.

gitops.detail.operation-gate.rationale: The provider-neutral detail surface renders server-observed operation gating and refresh/sync capability reasons without creating a browser command.

gitops.detail.revision-meta.rationale: The detail surface renders only the server-projected source revision; author and signature evidence remain a later provider integration.

gitops.graph-filter.input.rationale: Topology resource filtering must use the shared accessible input boundary and preserve the controlled query across graph updates.

gitops.list.operation-gate.rationale: Fleet row actions must make the operation-in-progress reason visible and must not submit a second conflicting Argo sync.

gitops.list.search-input.rationale: GitOps list search must remain a controlled, keyboard-accessible query without duplicating raw input behavior.

gitops.list.labels-input.rationale: Label search and AND-selection must preserve focus, outside dismissal, and the server-authorized row set.

gitops.managed-resources.disclosure.rationale: Managed-resource and kind disclosures must retain lazy content, resource navigation, and reduced-motion-safe state changes.

gitops.sync-countdown.duration.rationale: A controller-provided duration and observed timestamp must produce a safe countdown without browser-derived controller state.

gitops.sync-options.payload.rationale: Application and resource sync payloads must preserve selective-sync safety invariants and typed command identity at the adapter boundary.

gitops.sync-options.validation.rationale: Selective dry-run state, validation reset, operation gating, and outcome disclosure must be exercised through the product route.

gitops.sync-options.feedback.rationale: Dry-run success, failure, inconclusive, and redacted diagnostic feedback must be rendered from a typed server result.

gitops.insights.resource-diff.rationale: A revision-bound desired-versus-live diff must handle loading, redaction, errors, fullscreen dismissal, and no-change evidence.

gitops.insights.resource-filters.rationale: Resources search, OR facets, all-versus-declared inventory, apply order, and status sorting require route-level projection coverage.

gitops.insights.focus-disclosure.rationale: Issue-to-resource focus must clear incompatible local filters, scroll once, expand diagnostics, and respect reduced-motion preference.

gitops.insights.resource-actions.rationale: Resource open, missing-source navigation, selective sync eligibility, and inline drift/event disclosure must be capability-gated by the projection.

gitops.insights.availability.rationale: Application detail renders revision-bound comparison availability and an explicit unavailable reason without inventing a resource diff.

gitops.insights.helpers.rationale: Typed resource search, facet predicates, eligibility, and severity ordering must be deterministic outside rendering.

gitops.insights.status-summary.rationale: A synchronized but degraded resource must remain visible as degraded in the GitOps summary projection.

gitops.insights.disclosure-motion.rationale: Historical issue, raw-error, compact issue, and resource disclosures must retain semantic expanded state with reduced-motion-safe transitions.

gitops.tree.icon-and-portal.rationale: Topology node icons must use the shared resource registry and never make the root resource a recursive detail portal.

interactions.interaction: public timeline primitives compose through one product-owned route surface

opsiaPort.rationale: The product route already owns the shell and contract boundary; the upstream barrel is reference-only.

interactions.interaction: range, lens, and zoom-rung calculations keep a positive bounded selection

opsiaPort.blockedReason: TimelineCapabilityDescriptor does not yet describe lens minimums or server-approved zoom rungs.
opsiaPort.rationale: The browser must not invent range limits or a day-based zoom ladder.

interactions.interaction: pointer and keyboard lens changes clamp within the selected query range

motion.reducedMotion: range changes expose their final value without animated movement

opsiaPort.blockedReason: Server capability data for minimum lens window, keyboard step, and zoom rungs is absent.
opsiaPort.rationale: The retained strip must use descriptor values rather than hardcoded range arithmetic.

interactions.interaction: timeline marker and severity presentation remains semantically stable

opsiaPort.rationale: Current event cards already consume typed activity, event type, and severity values.

interactions.interaction: semantic event identity drives consistent list and lane markers

opsiaPort.rationale: Typed event labels and views are product-owned and do not import upstream renderers.

interactions.interaction: activity, kinds, deletion, search, and selected-event filters round-trip through URL state

opsiaPort.blockedReason: The server has no facet response to drive filter availability and independent counts.
opsiaPort.rationale: URL parsing exists, but dynamic toolbar choices must come from an authorized aggregation.

interactions.interaction: filter predicates use canonical activity and kind selections without client fixture data

opsiaPort.blockedReason: Facet aggregation and the server control catalog are not yet defined.
opsiaPort.rationale: Existing predicates accept filters, but the UI cannot safely infer selectable values or counts.

interactions.interaction: importance, recency, and name lane ordering is deterministic for one authorized projection

opsiaPort.blockedReason: The snapshot has events but no server lane aggregation or sort projection for large timelines.
opsiaPort.rationale: Client-only grouping would duplicate data logic and exceed smooth-update limits.

interactions.interaction: lane order follows a server-defined grouping and sort projection

opsiaPort.blockedReason: Grouping and sort enum values exist, but the backend does not emit a bounded lane projection.
opsiaPort.rationale: The product must not hardcode upstream lane ordering heuristics.

interactions.interaction: live and frozen range state preserves its cursor and reports unseen events

realtime.merge: bounded snapshot reducer keyed by source event identity

opsiaPort.blockedReason: The current stream has no overview-derived frozen-window unseen-event count.
opsiaPort.rationale: Snapshot and SSE behavior exist, while the Go-live affordance needs a truthful server count.

interactions.interaction: live selection advances through server sessions while frozen selection remains stable until Go live

realtime.merge: replace expired live sessions with a fresh bounded snapshot

motion.reducedMotion: live return updates selection without smooth scrolling

opsiaPort.blockedReason: The live default window and frozen-window update counter are not server-described.
opsiaPort.rationale: The client already follows a negotiated stream policy and must extend that policy rather than poll.

interactions.interaction: ordered events open a detail view using a ledger-unique selected event key

opsiaPort.rationale: The product list and detail sheet already use the typed sourceKey selection model.

interactions.interaction: query-range controls, histogram lens interaction, escape handling, and Go live are verified together

opsiaPort.blockedReason: No overview response or control descriptor exists to supply range presets, bucket data, and lens constraints.
opsiaPort.rationale: The strip cannot be tested honestly until its input data is server-owned.

interactions.interaction: range picker refetches selection while drag, resize, draw, and keyboard controls change a local lens

motion.reducedMotion: lens, live return, and calendar selection do not animate under reduced motion

opsiaPort.blockedReason: TimelineCapabilityDescriptor and snapshot contracts do not yet contain retained overview, preset, or lens descriptor fields.
opsiaPort.rationale: Selection and lens must be structurally separate and driven by server limits.

interactions.interaction: grouped lanes, pinned lanes, and pinned-only filtering honor capability and persisted user state

opsiaPort.blockedReason: There is no persisted pin contract and pinned_only is intentionally absent from server predicate and replay identity.
opsiaPort.rationale: A localStorage copy would be a false multi-workspace and multi-device implementation.

interactions.interaction: lane grouping, sorting, and pins present one stable timeline projection

motion.reducedMotion: lane updates retain final order without layout animation

opsiaPort.blockedReason: The service has no lane aggregation or authenticated user pin projection.
opsiaPort.rationale: Current swimlanes may show typed events, but cannot implement upstream pin semantics truthfully.

interactions.interaction: search, activity, kinds, deletion, view, sort, and overlay controls are keyboard and focus tested

opsiaPort.blockedReason: The server does not describe the control catalog or return facet counts for the toolbar.
opsiaPort.rationale: A hardcoded menu would diverge from the authorized data source.

interactions.interaction: slash search, escape, activity and problem chips, kinds picker, deleted filter, view menu, legend, and view toggle write canonical state

motion.reducedMotion: popover state and filter result changes remain legible without animated transitions

opsiaPort.blockedReason: Control availability, kind facets, activity counts, and pin capability are not server-described.
opsiaPort.rationale: The current URL state is reusable, but its controls must consume a strict descriptor and aggregation.

interactions.interaction: activity and problem controls project to canonical backend activity filters

opsiaPort.blockedReason: Activity source and problem projection availability are not part of the existing capability descriptor.
opsiaPort.rationale: The mapping must be verified against backend-defined activity semantics, not display text.

interactions.interaction: timeline source API requests preserve selected mode and retained-range behavior

realtime.backpressure: server negotiated max frames per second

opsiaPort.blockedReason: The overview endpoint and expanded control descriptor are not yet available at the Python API boundary.
opsiaPort.rationale: Existing adapter tests cover snapshot and stream; expanded requests require one typed API contract.

interactions.interaction: source transport reads retained history and live events without importing the upstream runtime

realtime.backpressure: server negotiated max frames per second

opsiaPort.rationale: The product already isolates HTTP and SSE behind a typed TimelinePort adapter.

interactions.interaction: local timeline source selects an explicit range without bypassing route capabilities

opsiaPort.rationale: Local versus retained source mode is already authenticated and capability-gated before route render.

interactions.interaction: retained-history overview renders bucketed evidence, coverage gaps, lens selection, and frozen-window new-event count

motion.reducedMotion: lens changes are direct and do not smooth-scroll under reduced motion

opsiaPort.blockedReason: Python currently returns coverage intervals but no retained overview buckets, facets, or frozen-window counter.
opsiaPort.rationale: The histogram must be rendered from authoritative aggregation, never synthesized from a capped event list.

interactions.interaction: web list rendering preserves selection and event navigation through URL state

opsiaPort.rationale: The current surface already restores event focus and uses the non-colliding source key.

interactions.interaction: timeline route composes source mode, URL state, filters, list or lanes, retained range, and live stream lifecycle

realtime.merge: bounded snapshot reducer with resync on invalid cursor

motion.reducedMotion: status and selection changes retain feedback without smooth scroll or layout motion

opsiaPort.blockedReason: The route lacks the server-described toolbar and retained overview contracts required for full parity.
opsiaPort.rationale: The existing route is the migration destination, but must retain its Python/SSE architecture rather than execute upstream code.

interactions.interaction: view, range, activity, kinds, deletion, pin, grouping, sort, and event keys restore through deep links and history

opsiaPort.blockedReason: pinnedOnly is currently inert because no authenticated pin contract or replay-identity revision exists.
opsiaPort.rationale: All other URL keys can remain reusable; pin state must not be claimed until it has server semantics.

interactions.interaction: a catalog or detail row exposes one typed batch signal badge and its explanatory tooltip only when the authorized projection supplies a signal

opsiaPort.rationale: The Python-owned batch runtime projection and shared catalog/detail channel now carry availability, completeness, status, and retained-run counters without browser inference; source-equivalent grouping and explanatory tooltip coverage remain in progress.

interactions.interaction: controlled application versus workload scope, overview/topology/history/cost selection, single-workload defaulting, and invalid workload recovery preserve the selected route state

opsiaPort.blockedReason: The current URL model has only overview/resources/deployments/drift/incidents and no typed workload scope, application topology, history, or optional cost projection contract.
opsiaPort.rationale: ApplicationsSurface.test.tsx already proves generic URL-backed detail navigation, but it cannot prove the new controlled scope rules until the missing projection and route state exist.

interactions.interaction: overview and history avoid duplicating current incidents, distinguish runtime from delivery health, preserve source provenance and conflicts, and report batch outcomes without treating idle jobs as serving failures

opsiaPort.rationale: Strict Python and Zod contracts now distinguish runtime, delivery, batch, source conflict, and bounded partial history; focused router, contract, adapter, and surface tests prove the implemented evidence while remaining source-specific interactions are tracked separately.

interactions.interaction: back navigation, controlled application/workload scope, overview/topology/history tabs, and an optional cost tab select exactly one application workspace without rendering workload runtime in app scope

motion.reducedMotion: tab and scope selection retain their final selected state without transform or color-transition motion when reduced motion is requested

opsiaPort.blockedReason: The current detail workspace has a different fixed five-tab model and no normalized workload key, app-scope topology/history view, or application-cost callback.
opsiaPort.rationale: ApplicationDetailWorkspace is the existing route owner and must be extended rather than importing the upstream shell.

interactions.interaction: overview combines operational issues, runtime and deployment delivery verdicts, restart warnings, workload matrix, retained batch activity, deployment-source provenance, and authorized entrypoint/dependency resource links

opsiaPort.rationale: The detail projection now supplies independent runtime, delivery, batch, source provenance/conflict, and server-authorized relationship evidence to the existing overview; workload-matrix and full source-specific navigation parity remain in progress.

interactions.interaction: authorized application topology colors workload ownership, hover-focuses the matching rail row, expands stable ReplicaSets, drills workload nodes into runtime, routes generated runs to their parent, routes related resources to detail, and labels deployment-source-only versus runtime-only resources

motion.reducedMotion: hover focus, legend selection, and ReplicaSet expansion remain immediate state changes without graph camera or layout animation under reduced motion

opsiaPort.rationale: The detail contract now renders server-authorized inventory graph nodes and ownership, scheduling, selector, or routing edges with completeness and freshness evidence; interactive graph focus, ReplicaSet expansion, and source-equivalent drilldowns remain in progress.

interactions.interaction: history exposes loading and partial-source state, current incidents, deployment anchors, retained latest-change or incident preview, direct workload navigation only for unambiguous objects, and source-view navigation without duplicate actions

opsiaPort.rationale: The detail contract now supplies ordered, bounded deployment and incident history with explicit partial-source reason codes and source provenance/conflict evidence; direct workload and source-view navigation remain in progress.

interactions.interaction: environment siblings switch among real application instances, show confidence/evidence and promotion lag, scale from inline pills to a searchable listbox, and dismiss scope/environment popovers on outside pointer or Escape

motion.reducedMotion: chevron rotation and color transitions are suppressed while popover open/close and selection remain fully perceivable under reduced motion

opsiaPort.rationale: The Python detail contract now projects only authorized immutable deployment-binding identities with workspace, cluster, namespace, and freshness evidence. The typed adapter and URL-backed selector scope detail, deployments, and drift reads to that server-selected identity; searchable large-list UX, promotion-lag evidence, and workload scope parity remain in progress.

interactions.interaction: catalog status strips, runtime cells, status facets, and ready-column sorting use batch runtime state for job apps while retaining serving readiness for non-job apps; grouped rows explain mixed runtime states in a tooltip

opsiaPort.rationale: Catalog cards and table rows now consume server-projected runtime, delivery, and batch-runtime evidence without browser inference; source-equivalent workload-class grouping and sort precedence remain in progress.

interactions.interaction: single and folded application rows show the highest-severity non-job batch signal with a shared explanatory tooltip while job rows present their runtime state instead

opsiaPort.rationale: Shared catalog surfaces now render one server-supplied batch-runtime channel with availability and completeness rather than deriving raw workload state; source-equivalent grouped highest-severity selection remains in progress.

interactions.interaction: catalog aggregation verifies delivery degradation overrides runtime-only display when appropriate and a successful retained batch outcome is not falsely presented as an unhealthy serving workload

opsiaPort.rationale: Python contract and projection tests plus adapter and surface tests now cover independent runtime, delivery, and retained batch evidence; the remaining source-specific aggregation precedence is still in progress.

interactions.interaction: a product-owned application detail boundary exposes a typed application view selection instead of coupling consumers to the source component implementation

opsiaPort.rationale: ApplicationDetailWorkspace already owns a typed private tab union and URL controller; it is the correct starting point for a reusable product boundary, although it does not yet expose source-equivalent views.

interactions.interaction: source selection and transport are composed outside individual timeline controls

realtime.merge: single TimelinePort stream ownership per read session

opsiaPort.rationale: Composition already occurs through TimelinePort and the capability-gated route factory.

interactions.interaction: an Argo sync action is disabled with a reason while an operation owns the application slot, while authorized refresh actions remain independently available

realtime.resume: resume the audited command stream from its durable operation cursor
realtime.backpressure: coalesce non-terminal progress updates per command attempt
realtime.merge: accept terminal state only when command, attempt, resource identity, and scope match

opsiaPort.rationale: The provider-neutral detail projection now carries a typed GitOpsApplication ResourceRef, observed Opsia workflow gate, and separate authorized refresh/sync capability reasons. Both commands remain disabled until a provider-neutral audited CommandReceipt executor and event stream exist.

interactions.interaction: the detail status strip can render host-supplied commit author and signature metadata beside the exact latest revision

opsiaPort.rationale: The detail projection now carries only an observed source revision, bound to the application detail response. Commit author, signature, and controller provenance remain unavailable rather than inferred in the browser.

interactions.interaction: a shared controlled text input filters an authorized GitOps topology while preset and facet callbacks remain owned by the route

opsiaPort.blockedReason: Opsia has a reusable accessible input primitive but no GitOps topology route, typed tree projection, or graph filter state to consume it.
opsiaPort.rationale: The generic Input is not evidence of source-equivalent resource filtering until it is connected to a server-authorized GitOps tree.

interactions.interaction: an Argo fleet-row Sync action exposes an operation-in-progress reason and refuses a conflicting second sync while keeping refresh semantics separate

realtime.resume: resume each row command from the command receipt cursor
realtime.backpressure: coalesce progress events by command attempt without losing a terminal event
realtime.merge: merge only events whose scope and immutable resource reference equal the open row

opsiaPort.blockedReason: GitOpsSyncTableView lists deployment bindings and polling status only; it does not receive Argo operation phase, per-resource capabilities, or row command receipts.
opsiaPort.rationale: The row must be driven by the same server operation state as the detail action, never by local pending flags alone.

interactions.interaction: the fleet search field remains a controlled shared input for application, repository, and path filtering

opsiaPort.blockedReason: The existing sync table has no application/repository/path query state and its adapter cannot project the controller fields searched by the source view.
opsiaPort.rationale: Filtering must operate on a typed GitOps catalog projection, not on browser-normalized unknown payloads.

interactions.interaction: the labels popup autofocuses a controlled search, combines selected labels with AND semantics, clears selection, and dismisses outside the popup

opsiaPort.blockedReason: No GitOps catalog contract exposes authorized labels, label facet counts, or a stable row identity for the current sync table.
opsiaPort.rationale: A local label dropdown would silently invent a client-only subset and cannot be considered an equivalent fleet filter.

interactions.interaction: managed-resource and kind disclosures lazily mount grouped inventory, retain show-all state, and expose expanded state with a shared collapse affordance

motion.reducedMotion: disclosure state remains visible while the port disables nonessential expand and chevron animation under reduced motion

opsiaPort.blockedReason: No GitOps detail inventory projection or managed-resource identity exists in the current Python and React GitOps boundary.
opsiaPort.rationale: Lazy disclosure must be layered over controller inventory, not reconstructed from release-plan steps.

interactions.interaction: a managed resource invokes route-owned resource navigation and exposes that affordance only when a destination exists

opsiaPort.blockedReason: Current GitOps data has no Kubernetes ResourceRef/UID per inventory item and therefore cannot navigate safely to an authorized resource drawer.
opsiaPort.rationale: Navigation needs immutable resource identity rather than a display name and namespace string.

interactions.interaction: a controller-provided reconciliation interval and observed sync time produce a resilient countdown that treats imminent work as a distinct state

motion.reducedMotion: the imminent indicator remains distinguishable without pulse animation

opsiaPort.blockedReason: GitOpsSyncTarget exposes poll observation time but not controller reconciliation interval, suspended state, or an authoritative next-run value.
opsiaPort.rationale: The browser must only count down from server-projected controller facts and cannot invent a reconciliation schedule.

interactions.interaction: tests prove selective resource sync strips revision, prune, and apply-only fields while retaining typed force and sync-option choices

opsiaPort.blockedReason: The GitOps port defines release-plan actions only and has no typed Argo application or selective resource-sync command payload.
opsiaPort.rationale: The safety invariant belongs at the product adapter and Python command contract before a dialog can submit it.

interactions.interaction: full application sync and selective resource sync expose distinct options, reset stale form state on open, and prevent resource sync from enabling prune, revision, or apply-only semantics

realtime.resume: resume the resulting command by CommandReceipt audit cursor
realtime.backpressure: retain each terminal validation or execution state and coalesce intermediate progress
realtime.merge: apply status only to the dialog whose application and resource ResourceRef match the receipt

opsiaPort.blockedReason: There is no server endpoint or typed CommandRequest for Argo application/resource sync, no resource identity, and no capability check for selective sync in the current GitOps domain.
opsiaPort.rationale: The dialog cannot reuse generic release-plan submission because Argo selective sync has materially different safety fields and scope.

interactions.interaction: a selective dry-run shows pending, succeeded, failed, inconclusive, and server-error states, resets stale validation after option changes, and keeps execution gated while an operation is active

realtime.resume: reconnect a validation or command operation using its durable receipt cursor
realtime.backpressure: coalesce progress but preserve the final outcome and redacted diagnostic evidence
realtime.merge: reject events whose receipt, resource identity, or validation generation differs from the open dialog

opsiaPort.blockedReason: Current release-plan readiness is plan-level and has no resource-scoped dry-run receipt, outcome enum, redacted diagnostic payload, or operation conflict state.
opsiaPort.rationale: A client-side success banner would be false; validation feedback must originate from an audited server/agent operation.

interactions.interaction: an authorized desired-versus-live resource diff renders loading, error, no-change, secret-masked, inline, and fullscreen states; outside click and Escape close the fullscreen overlay

motion.reducedMotion: the loading skeleton and fullscreen transition render a stable non-animated state when reduced motion is requested

opsiaPort.blockedReason: domains.gitops.diffing handles repository patch workflows, not an authenticated Argo desired/live resource-diff projection; no frontend GitOps detail surface or immutable resource scope exists.
opsiaPort.rationale: Diff body, masking, revision, and live-observation provenance must be supplied by Python/agent contracts rather than assembled from browser YAML.

interactions.interaction: revision provenance is rendered beside a health summary that does not mask degraded resources as synchronized, while historical issue and raw-error disclosures retain semantic expanded state

motion.reducedMotion: collapse content and chevrons preserve expanded state without animated transitions under reduced motion

opsiaPort.blockedReason: The current page has release-plan readiness and feedback, not a GitOps resource summary, controller issue history, health evidence, or revision provenance projection.
opsiaPort.rationale: Summary normalization and disclosure state must consume one typed detail response so one controller failure is not fabricated as many client-side issues.

interactions.interaction: the resources surface switches declared versus all inventory, searches name/kind/namespace/group, OR-filters OutOfSync/Degraded/Missing, resets filters, and sorts by apply order, resource, sync, or health

opsiaPort.blockedReason: No current GitOps contract carries controller-declared resources, generated descendants, apply wave/order, normalized sync/health, drift, or event fields.
opsiaPort.rationale: Only route-owned local view state may filter a complete server-authorized resource set; the browser may not synthesize inventory from workflow steps.

interactions.interaction: an issue deep-link clears incompatible filters, scrolls once to and expands the matching row, then exposes structured drift, recent events, live-resource navigation, or source navigation for a missing resource

motion.reducedMotion: focus navigation preserves the selected row and disclosure without smooth scrolling when reduced motion is active

opsiaPort.blockedReason: Opsia has no GitOps issue-to-ResourceRef relation, per-resource drift/events, or safe source-link projection for a missing live resource.
opsiaPort.rationale: The focus target must use immutable resource identity and capability-gated destinations, not a name-only browser search.

interactions.interaction: the page truthfully distinguishes Argo diff availability, connection/setup guidance, comparison-unavailable sync state, ignored-difference coverage, and a lazily mounted full resource diff

opsiaPort.rationale: The application-detail contract now reports revision-bound desired/live comparison availability and reason codes, and the UI renders the unavailable state without a browser diff. Controller connection guidance, ignored-difference coverage, and resource diff content remain a later provider integration.

interactions.interaction: only declared, non-hook, OutOfSync or Missing Argo resources expose selective sync; disabled reasons are shown without removing the action

realtime.resume: resume the resource command from its durable receipt cursor
realtime.backpressure: coalesce non-terminal command updates while preserving cancellation and terminal facts
realtime.merge: attach an event only when its ResourceRef, application identity, scope, and command attempt match the row

opsiaPort.blockedReason: There is no GitOps resource eligibility projection, Argo application ownership proof, or resource-scoped command endpoint in the existing Python contracts.
opsiaPort.rationale: Eligibility and disabled reasons are server authority decisions; they cannot be recreated from browser status strings.

interactions.interaction: the GitOps insights boundary exports the resource diff viewer without requiring consumers to import an isolated upstream runtime path

opsiaPort.blockedReason: No product-owned GitOps insight or diff component boundary exists because the corresponding route and contracts have not been ported.
opsiaPort.rationale: The eventual export must be product-owned and consume the GitOpsPort, never re-export code from references/upstream.

interactions.interaction: tests cover normalized status severity, search and OR-facet predicates, independent resource counts, selective-sync eligibility, and urgency sort order

opsiaPort.blockedReason: No equivalent typed GitOps resource model exists in frontend/src/features/gitops, so these predicates cannot be tested without embedding source-shaped unknown records.
opsiaPort.rationale: Pure helper tests are added only after the Python projection defines the resource fields they normalize.

interactions.interaction: resource status normalization keeps sync and health independent, applies OR facets, ranks urgent states first, and excludes generated or hook resources from selective sync

opsiaPort.blockedReason: Release-plan workflow models do not contain controller resource sync, health, hook, generated, or desired/live fields needed for these pure predicates.
opsiaPort.rationale: The port must normalize a Python-owned GitOps resource projection instead of casting arbitrary controller payloads in the browser.

interactions.interaction: topology search uses the shared controlled input and node kind presentation uses a shared resource-icon registry rather than CSS class name construction

opsiaPort.blockedReason: The current GitOps route has no topology graph, typed node kind registry, or controller-tree query to bind to the existing shared input primitive.
opsiaPort.rationale: A product tree must use a centralized resource icon registry and typed node kinds, never source CSS selectors or a browser-derived graph.

interactions.interaction: a GitOps-managed child node may offer a detail portal, but the root node is explicitly excluded so the current detail page cannot recursively navigate to itself

opsiaPort.blockedReason: There is no GitOps detail route or typed tree node role in Opsia, so current navigation cannot distinguish a root subject from a managed child portal.
opsiaPort.rationale: This invariant must be encoded in the eventual route model before child GitOps CR navigation is exposed.
